messages.author: 253141a6efac547e
messages.subject: inspect(fit, "data")?
parts: To look at my covariance matrix of my data, I often use inspect(fit, "sample") - is there a similar argument to get the data used to fit the model?  Might be great in combination with pairs to actually view the underlying behavior of what's going on - and, heck, even pull out coefficients to generate residuals of the data and such in observed variable models.

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: inspect(fit, "data")?
parts:
On 07/02/2013 06:03 PM, Jarrett Byrnes wrote:
> To look at my covariance matrix of my data, I often use inspect(fit,
> "sample") - is there a similar argument to get the data used to fit
> the model?

Sure!

inspect(fit, "data") is now available in dev 0.5-14.

Might be great in combination with pairs to actually view
> the underlying behavior of what's going on

also in dev 0.5-14: pairs(fit) produces a pairs plot (byd default for
the first group only; use pairs(fit, group=2) for the second, ...)

and, heck, even pull out
> coefficients to generate residuals of the data and such in observed
> variable models.

again, in dev 0.5-14:

resid(fit, "casewise") (or resid(fit, "obs"))

should give you 'raw' casewise residuals.

Yves.

parts:
FYI, the casewise residuals appears to be broken

residuals(fit, "casewise")
Error in ETA[[g]] %*% t(LAMBDA) : non-conformable arguments


This from

x<-seq(-1,1,.01)
y1 <- rnorm(length(x), x)
y2 <- rnorm(length(x), y1+2*x)

adf <- data.frame(x=x, y1=y1, y2=y2)

mod <- '
y1 ~ x
y2 ~ x+y1
'

fit <- sem(mod, adf)

residuals(fit, "casewise")
